problem: The join returns Matched on a one-word coincidence and prints rule text for a feature the character does not have. The SCOPED tier accepts any candidate sharing `class_slug` + 1 word, with no requirement that the match explain the rest of the tail; and the collapsed-tail arm credits `coverage = original_tail_len` (the WHOLE tail) when it merely consumes the collapsed tail, which inflates a partial match into a unique winner instead of None/Ambiguous. Three confirmed-wrong joins in the live 313-build population, all `before=None -> after=Matched`, all `print=true`.
evidence: `class_feature.untabled.magus.magus_arcana.pool` -> `ultimate_magic:class_feature:magus_arcana_pool_strike` (build magus:20). Traced onto the real sheet: `<scratch>/sheets/after/magus_L20.txt:99 HELD| ultimate_magic:class_feature:magus_arcana_pool_strike` and `:148 LINE| ... label=Pool Strike`. `dump-after/ultimate_magic/class_feature/magus_arcana_pool_strike.json` has `granted_by: null`, and it is the ONLY one of ~50 `magus_arcana_*` records held on that sheet — the facet join is the sole cause. Mechanism: collapsed tail [arcana, pool] fully consumed -> coverage promoted from 2 to 3, beating every honest competitor. Also `class_feature.acg.skald.raging_climber` and `.raging_swimmer` -> `advanced_class_guide:class_feature:skald_raging_song` (build skald:20, print=true, before=None) on a 1-word 'raging' prefix, while the correct records `rage_power_raging_climber` / `rage_power_raging_swimmer` exist in the package; my oracle shows `raging_leaper` does the same. 56 of the 952 matched facets are this shape (scoped match on <=1 common word with both sides diverging); most are benign, these are not.
fix: Require the scoped tier to consume the tail the same way the bare tier does, or at minimum refuse a Matched when the match explains strictly less than the tail AND the candidate has its own unexplained words (return Ambiguous/None instead — both are already safe outcomes). Drop the collapsed-tail full-credit promotion, or cap it at `matched_collapsed_words`. Add the magus/skald pairs as RED tests against the real package.

section: 2 — Join / bare tier 'never the principal' invariant
problem: The bare tier has no principal-rule guard and can return the class's own principal rule — the exact outcome spec 3b.2 says the function must refuse 'under any circumstance'. The code comment asserting the guard is unnecessary is provably wrong.
evidence: Oracle probe (validated 0-mismatch against the Rust join): `rule_for_explanation(pkg, "fighter", "class_feature.fighter.fighter")` -> `Matched(core_rulebook:class_feature:fighter)`, the class principal. The scoped tier has `if slug == class_slug { continue }`; the bare tier has no such check, and its comment claims 'a bare class-slug-only candidate could never fully consume a real (non-empty) tail' — false whenever a tail segment equals the class slug, which the sliding window makes reachable from any id with a later segment named after the class. Tests `a_facet_id_never_joins_to_the_class_principal_rule` and `class_slug_alone_is_never_a_valid_match_length` only exercise the scoped path, so nothing pins this.
fix: Add `if slug == class_slug { continue }` to the bare-tier loop and a RED test for `class_feature.<class>.<class>` and for a nested window landing on a class-named segment.

problem: `builds_scanned=313` is stated but is not the population the report describes. The report's own `population` string says 'every prestige class's first-named carrier @ own max_level'; 7 prestige classes are silently `continue`d before `builds += 1`, never counted, never named, and never scanned.
evidence: 313 = 61 non-prestige + 67 prestige + 185 mix. The census itself has `prestige_swept=74` (`docs/release/SD-36-consolidation/artifacts/epic-f/README.md:42`, and `census-f0c.json['prestige']` has 74 rows, all 74 with a non-empty `carrier`). Deriving the prestige slugs present in `duplicates-after.json` rows gives 67; the 7 missing are dark_tempest, dragon_disciple, elocater, evangelist, psion_uncarnate, pure_legion_enforcer, thrallherd. Cause: `let Some(gate) = prestige_applies_gate(..) else { continue }` / `let Ok(carriers) = determine_carriers(..) else { continue }` / `carriers.into_iter().next()` drop them with no count and no diagnostic — an unnamed remainder inside the instrument that is supposed to prove the join safe.
fix: Count and name the skipped prestige classes in `DuplicateScanReport` (e.g. `prestige_skipped: Vec<String>`), print them in the one-line summary, and correct the `population` string and the receipt's §2 denominator to '67 of 74 prestige carriers (7 named, no carrier determinable)'.

problem: The re-run is presented as evidence about the join, but it cannot observe the join at all: both the BEFORE and the AFTER halves were rendered with the R2 join already in the tree, so the only variable is the package. Every one of the 607 newly-matched facets is present identically on both sides and therefore contributes nothing to `added_correct`/`duplicate`/`changed_value`. No instrument in stage 4 checks the correctness of a single new match.
evidence: `<scratch>/sheets/before/magus_L20.txt:99` and `sheets/after/magus_L20.txt:99` both carry `HELD| ultimate_magic:class_feature:magus_arcana_pool_strike` — the wrong join is invisible to the classifier by construction. `sheets/before/*` are timestamped 21:18, after the R2 code landed. This is the same delta-only blind spot the receipt itself names for the Rage values ('nothing differed, so stage-3's original delta-only methodology reported changed_value=0 while the true value was silently wrong on both sides'), but it is not applied to the join's own evidence. `class_census --duplicates` counts transitions only; it never asks whether a new Matched target is the right rule.
fix: Render a genuine pre-R2 baseline (HEAD~1 binary, tracked package) against the post-R2 binary on the same package, and classify that delta — that is the only diff that measures R2. Separately, hand-audit a stated sample of the 607 new matches (with the sample size and seed named) for target correctness before the population run.

problem: Spec 3b.2 requires the frontend and `HeldSeed::from_character` to use ONE join. Stage 4 changed the Rust half and left the TypeScript half on the old exact-slug walk, so each of the 607 newly-joined facets now prints its rule line in 'Rules and features' AND keeps its 'not computed' notice in 'Class Features' — the same feature shown twice, one of the two saying it was not computed.
evidence: `classFeaturesModel.ts` still builds `candidates = [`${classToken}_${feature}`, feature]` and requires an exact slug equality against the rendered lines — the pre-R2 algorithm, verbatim. For `class_feature.acg.brawler.knockout_dc` the Rust join now holds and prints `brawler_knockout`, while the TS candidates are `brawler_knockout_dc`/`knockout_dc`, so the notice is retained. Before stage 4 the two agreed (both matched exactly the same 514 facets); the desync is newly created here. `dedup-receipt.md` §5 names it as out-of-scope follow-up, which is honest but does not make the shipped desktop consistent.
fix: Either carry the join's `rule_id` on the DTO and have `noticeHasSheetRule` compare that (the spec's own instruction, 'no new wire field'), or hold this commit's desktop-visible half until the TS side lands. If it must ship desynced, say so explicitly in the epic status, not only in an artifact receipt.
